[00:00] Ava: ok, hey everyone, uh welcome to the January all hands, thanks for joining, we got a lot to cover so we'll kick off with Q4 numbers real quick then product news and then Q&A, uh quick note we recorded this for folks who couldn't make it.
[01:12] Ethan: quick finance update, Q4 ARR grew 18% q/q, net retention held at ~112%, we saw stronger-than-expected adoption in mid-market, margin improved a bit on batching and caching wins in production, uh some one-time infra costs hitting year-end, overall healthy. (inaudible)
[02:05] Ava: appreciate that, big shout to Eng and SRE for getting the Dedicated throughput improvements in, customers noticed latency consistency.
[03:30] Liam: on the tech side, short version, we've shipped micro-optimizations to the runtime kernels, improved KV cache eviction heuristics, and changed default batching thresholds which reduces p99 by ~15% in our internal benchmarks, again these numbers vary by model. we also have early perf profiles for the new quantized variants.
[05:00] Priya: product update: Private is technically GA for a handful of customers, we will open the self-serve onboarding next month, docs launching this week, note that Private includes VPC peering, customer-managed KMS/hsm integration, and audit log export. there are some limitations in the first wave: autoscaling is limited to pre-provisioned bursts, and certain older models don't have optimized kernels yet.
[06:40] Crowd: (applause, scattered)
[07:00] Jamal: small note from eng - rolling out stronger monitoring on KV cache hit rates and adding more traces so we can surface regresses earlier, also working on a bug where cold-start on large sequence lengths causes a spike in token latency, have a mitigation in staging.
[08:45] Ava: customer wins - we closed Acme Financial, NovaBank pilot moved to production, and a fintech ISV signed an initial Dedicated commitment. these are strategic because they show both hosted and dedicated buying patterns.
[10:10] Sofia: sales notes - pipeline is healthy, conversion times shortened with our benchmark kit; we need updated one-pagers showing the economics of Dedicated vs Hosted, customers keep asking about the break-even point when Dedicated makes sense.
[12:00] Audience (Q): can you elaborate on pricing, uh the break-even numbers?
[12:20] Ethan: sure, rough rule of thumb - for steady sustained throughput above ~X tokens per month (notes: internal benchmark spreadsheet), Dedicated becomes economical vs hosted, but it depends on model selection and sequence length, we'll share a calc model.
[13:36] Priya: we will publish an interactive calculator, yes. also note Optimize recommendations are now live in beta for selected accounts to suggest batching and quantization policy.
[15:00] (transcription glitch) Speaker 1: uh Redwood inferencing.. redwoood? heh..
[15:30] Liam: haha, we hear it, but yes, the product name gets mangled sometimes in the transcript.
[16:00] Ava: security/compliance update - we're SOC 2 Type II in final review, ISO 27001 audit kickoff scheduled for next quarter, implemented RBAC improvements, and KMS integration tested with two customers, some audit logs formatting work remains.
[18:30] Jamal: addendum - for Private/on-prem we have additional checklist items to validate HSM path and network egress controls; please see the security playbook doc we linked in the announcement.
[20:00] Audience question: any updates on on-prem (air-gapped) package?
[20:20] Priya: yes, the on-prem package is in alpha; it's intended for regulated customers with strict data residency, but we are limiting the first release to a set of partners to reduce support surface.

[27:10] Audience: question about Dedicated autoscaling vs predictable commit - how does that work?
[27:40] Jamal: good question, we offer Dedicated reserved pools for baseline throughput and a burst policy that can use shared capacity for transient spikes; the tradeoff is cost predictability vs absolute lowest latency. we recommend hybrid routing for many customers.
[29:00] Priya: also worth mentioning the routing policies: latency-priority vs cost-priority, automatic fallback to compatible model variants. we' re collecting feedback on the defaults.
[31:20] Audience: is there a plan to surface more per-route cost analytics in the console?
[31:45] Liam: yes, console v2 will include per-route token breakdown and tail latency histograms (in beta for internal accounts), and the tracing hooks will let you tie traces to specific requests for debugging.
